channel.title: Your Impossible Voice - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Your Impossible Voice (yourimpossiblevoice.com)

item.title: The Ants | Your Impossible Voice
item.description: Holly Lyn Walrath — "You lie in the grass and let ants crawl all over you. You lie so perfectly still that they start to think you’re just another part of the landscape—a rock, a log, a statue."

item.title: Two Funerals | Your Impossible Voice
item.description: Toshiya Kamei — The phone call had come that morning. Etsuko’s sister-in-law, Akiko, her voice thin and stretched tight as a wire. “Kenji passed,” she’d said, no preamble, no softening.

item.title: Girl Crushed – 1985 | Your Impossible Voice
item.description: Phyllis Rittner — In the office kitchen, all lashes and cheekbones, gift-wrapped cozy in your cashmere sweater, peeling an orange like a surgeon, sectioning each sliver, the way you segment our time, a juicy burst here and there, little pink hearts dotting your calendar.

item.title: Ignoring Poetic Schools: Premeditations by Klipschutz | Your Impossible Voice
item.description: Review by Art Beck — This book has been out for a half dozen years and was well received for a small press volume. But I just came across it a few weeks ago and was so happy to read it that I feel compelled to publicly respond with my thanks to the one-named San Francisco poet, Klipschutz.

item.title: Squirrel Fish | Your Impossible Voice
item.description: Ann Yuan — I meet my future husband on the eve of the Lunar New Year. A forty-seven-year-old Beijing native: a decent job, two apartments, recently divorced, and seeking a stepmother for his preteen son—my auntie posted only this much in the family WeChat group.

item.title: Corrine, Edna, and Imogene: A Family of Good Women by Teddy Jones | Your Impossible Voice
item.description: Review by Peter Mladinic — Against the backdrop of this male-dominated world, Imogene raises her voice, as she ponders fundamental questions: What is family? Where is home? Who am I?

item.title: Detention Seeds | Your Impossible Voice
item.description: Brandon McNeice — We had planned for this. In our pockets: sunflower, cosmos, zinnia, marigold. Milkweed fluff, Kiki said her grandmother called silk. The seeds came from wherever kids get things—bodega packets, porch planters, the torn corner of a springtime display.

item.title: Big Brother Says “2 + 2 = Fun” |
item.description: By T.S. Carney — I was listening to NPR, a favorite pastime of my family (including my nearly two-year-old son). At seven o’clock in our region, we hear the show 1A — a program that tackles the issues of the day, earnestly and without irony.

item.title: The Falling Stars: “Not Diminishing the Sacred Number” of Rilke’s Uncollected Poems | Essays
item.description: By Wally Swist — "In Rilke’s praises, we find our own praise—of ourselves, of others, of mostly anything, actually. When anyone experiences an epiphany, that person wants to share that epiphany."

item.title: Scrap: Salvaging a Family by Luanne Castle | Your Impossible Voice
item.description: Review by Wilma J. Kahn — A memoir in flash, Scrap focuses on three discrete parts of Castle’s life in relation to her parents, especially her father. “Scrap” is a multivalent word, and around each of its meanings and nuances, Castle fashions poignant—and sometimes horrifying—flash prose and poetry that reveal her family in all its human pain, mystery, and love.

item.title: The Fence is Always Hungry | Your Impossible Voice
item.description: By Claudia Monpere — We feed it raw chicken three times a day, but it is never enough. The fence is always changing.
